# Audio licence notes

**No third-party recorded audio is shipped with WAHALA!.** Every file here was generated by this
project's own scripts, and every other sound is synthesised at runtime by `src/audio/recipes` (pure
DSP, no samples). This file also exists so that anyone who adds a recording records where it came from.

| What | Files | How it was made | Licence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Afrobeats music loops and stings | `music/*` | Original composition, written as note data in `tools/audiogen/compose_*.py` and rendered with numpy/scipy synthesis (plucked-string models, FM electric piano, additive pads, percussion models). No samples, no existing songs or melodies. | Project-owned original work |
| Pidgin voice clips (**synthetic placeholders**) | `voices/*` | Kokoro-82M neural text-to-speech (Apache-2.0 model; outputs may be used freely) driven by hand-written Pidgin pronunciations (`tools/audiogen/pidgin_script.py`). Not recordings of people. | Project-owned generated audio; model Apache-2.0 |
| Lagos ambience beds | `crowd_loop.*`, `buspark_loop.*`, `crowd_loop_hype.*` | Babble assembled from the synthetic Pidgin clips plus synthesised engines, generators, horns and clanks (`tools/audiogen/build_ambience.py`). | Project-owned generated audio |

Tools used offline only (nothing is shipped to players): Python, numpy, scipy, pyloudnorm, ffmpeg,
kokoro-onnx (+ its model files), sherpa-onnx with Whisper-small.en (only to run a rough readability
check on the synthetic speech).

For every file you add to this folder, add a row here (and a matching `license` field in
`slots.json`, which the game requires before it will use a recording):

| Slot | File | What it is | Author / source URL | Licence (name + link) | Date obtained | Attribution text required? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _none yet_ | | | | | | |

Rules of thumb:

- Only add recordings you are allowed to redistribute inside a public GitHub Pages build
  (CC0, CC-BY with attribution shown, or purchased with a licence that permits redistribution in a
  game). "Free to download" is not a licence.
- Do not label a recording as something it is not (for example, do not describe a stock crowd track
  as "recorded in Lagos" unless that is documented by the source).
- Keep the original licence text or receipt alongside the project records.
